events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
The rider alleges the driver took a different route and that the meter ran to 12 km against a 7 km estimate [F2]. The trace confirms a large measured deviation: an off-route segment 09:04–09:14 drove 5.23 km where the optimal route covers 1.08 km, adding 4.15 km and reaching up to 1989 m from the optimal route [F4], and the fare record shows excess distance billed at $7.04 (4.99 km × $1.4100/km) [F5]. No exemption is available on the record: there are no traffic incidents near the route during the trip window [F14], and the only speed-band records are at EU TONG SEN STREET and SENTOSA GATEWAY at band 3 [F12][F13], which under RD-4(b) does not excuse a segment on its own and does not match the driven deviation.

The whole chat record is two timestamped messages, both about pickup logistics [F8][F9][F10]; nothing in it is a rider route choice or an agreement to any route change. The driver's written statement claims merely that the GPS rerouted him [F11]; under RD-5 the route change must be proposed by the driver before leaving the optimal route and accepted by the rider before the segment, and a post-trip statement is not rider consent — so no segment is exempt under RD-3 or RD-5.

However, RD-1's precondition is a measurable off-route segment, and the trace does not cover the whole trip: the last GPS sample is 4 min 0 s before the 09:20:45 drop-off, and what happened outside the covered stretch is not on record [F1]. The uncovered stretch is itself off the measured window, and the measured distance figures (10.2 km actual vs 7.2 km optimal; 12.17 km on the meter) cannot be reconciled within the covered trace alone, so the excess on which any RD-2 amount would rest is not fully settled [F1][F2][F7]. Where a record a clause needs is missing, the matter goes to a person; the outcome cannot be computed on this record [RD-1][RD-2].

Safety screen: I read every message, the complaint and the driver's statement [F8][F9][F11]. The complaint is a fare/route grievance, the chat is a pickup arrangement, and the driver's statement is a bare denial; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11]. Safety concern: none.

Because the measurement is incomplete, no refund amount can be stated, and the trace's ✗ on GPS coverage settles the evidence question, not the merits. The rider's claim of an unnotified detour is supported as far as it is measurable [F4][F5], but the driver's account cannot be tested against an uncovered stretch the record does not show [F1][F11]; both positions therefore remain open and the case goes to human review.
